extracted.intended_audience: ARIPO patent applicants, their representatives, and ARIPO formalities/examining staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and formal requirements and standards for filing, formal examination, correction, publication, divisional filings, biological/sequence disclosures, and PCT-entering-ARIPO phase matters under the Harare Protocol as implemented by ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title must state technical designation
rubrics_metrics.description: The title must clearly state the technical designation of the invention and must exclude all fancy names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal names, fancy names, the word "patent" or similar non-technical terms which do not serve to identify the invention should not be used; trade names and trademarks should also not be used; titles such as "Method", "Apparatus", "Chemical Compounds" alone or similar vague titles do not meet the requirement. The abbreviation "etc." should not be used and should be replaced by an indication of what it is intended to cover. The Formality Section should avoid publication of clearly non-informative or misleading titles and, in obvious non-compliance, ARIPO may change the title of its own motion and notify the applicant only at publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for title compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ultimate responsibility for ensuring the title accords with the Implementing Regulations rests with the Examining Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Formality Section should still act to avoid publication of clearly non-informative or misleading titles and take cognizance of Harare Protocol provisions; ARIPO may change titles without immediate applicant notification and only notify the applicant when the application is about to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every application for a patent must contain an abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no abstract is provided, ARIPO shall invite the applicant to correct the deficiency either by providing an abstract or by paying the prescribed fee for ARIPO to prepare the abstract itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Contracting States must be valid at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: All States designated must be Contracting States to the Harare Protocol at the filing date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other State entered on the request for grant must be disregarded. See General Part for list of ARIPO Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling insufficient designation fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If designation fees paid during grace periods are insufficient, establish how many states are covered by the sum paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite applicant to inform ARIPO for which Contracting States the fees are to be used, or ARIPO will apply the sum to the first designated states as indicated on the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deemed withdrawn for non-payment of designation fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no designation fee is validly paid by expiry of the grace periods, the application is deemed to be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surrender of priority claims thereafter does not alter the position. Notification and legal consequences follow as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation fee consequences and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Loss of rights arises on expiry of the normal period if application deemed withdrawn for failure to pay designation fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deemed withdrawal of a designation of a Contracting State takes effect upon expiry of the normal period (not the period of grace). Applicant is notified where contrary to originally declared intention he failed to pay designation fees for states he intended to cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Grant must contain designations and may pay fees within 21 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The designation of Contracting States where protection is desired shall be contained in the request for grant; designation fees may be paid on filing or within 21 days from filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of prescribed Request for Grant with pre-crossed declaration designating all ARIPO Contracting States at filing ensures all designations are made on filing day and gives applicant time to decide by paying designation fees for chosen states. A designation may be withdrawn up to grant but the fee is not refunded. Withdrawal of all states results in deemed withdrawal of the application. A designation may not be withdrawn once a third party proves they initiated entitlement proceedings and until ARIPO resumes proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARIPO-PCT entry: designation fees timing and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: For ARIPO-PCT applications entering the ARIPO phase, designation fees must be paid upon entry or within 21 days from entry date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-payment in time leads to deemed withdrawal of designation(s) or the ARIPO patent application. If ARIPO finds deemed withdrawal occurred it informs the applicant; loss of rights is deemed not to have occurred if the omitted act is performed within two months from notification. Applicant may request extension of time subject to payment of extension request fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of deficiencies: opportunity to remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Where during examination deficiencies which may be corrected are found, the Formalities Section must give the applicant opportunity to rectify each deficiency within a specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Formalities Section should raise all formal objections evident from first examination in its first report. If applicant required to appoint a representative and has not done so, the first report should cover that and other obvious deficiencies, assuming applicant will appoint a representative within the allowed period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods for remedying deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: ARIPO determines periods for remedying listed deficiencies; such periods must not be less than 2 months and not more than 4 months, generally set at 2 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficiencies include non-appointment of representative or failure to file authorization; documents not complying with physical requirements; request for grant not satisfactory (except priority criteria); abstract not filed; missing priority document/file number/translation. Failure to correct within time results in refusal (cases i-iv) or loss of rights (cases v-vi), and the applicant is notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application filing: parent pending requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any pending ARIPO patent application may be divided; the parent application must be pending when a divisional is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent may be any kind of application (including earlier divisional). For ARIPO-PCT parent, divisional may be filed only once ARIPO-PCT application is pending before ARIPO (entered ARIPO phase). If parent was deemed withdrawn due to non-observance of a time limit, it is no longer pending unless loss of rights is remedied (further processing, re-establishment) or appeal delays effect. Once refused, divisional cannot be filed unless notice of appeal is filed and appeal proceedings keep refusal from taking effect. Divisional may be filed while appeal proceedings are under way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the applicant on record may file a divisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application was transferred, a divisional may only be filed by or on behalf of the new applicant if the transfer was duly registered and effective at the filing date of the divisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of filing of divisional and content limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application may be filed in respect of subject-matter which does not extend beyond the content of the parent application as filed and is deemed filed on the parent's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided requirement met, divisional enjoys parent filing date and priority. Whether it is confined to subject-matter of parent is decided during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority for divisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A priority claimed in the parent application may apply also to the divisional application; divisional retains that priority provided the parent's priority claim has not lapsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary to claim priority again. If priority documents and translations were filed for parent before filing divisional, they need not be filed again; ARIPO copies them into divisional file. If priority documents weren't filed for parent when divisional is filed, they must be filed for divisional (and for parent if priority to be retained). If divisional relates only to some of the priorities claimed in parent, priority documents need be filed only for those priorities; same applies to indicating file number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file a divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application must be filed directly to ARIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing with a national authority has no legal effect though the authority may forward as a service; not deemed received until filed at ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for grant for divisional must state relation
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for grant of a divisional must contain a statement that a divisional application is sought and state the number of the parent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If request is deficient (no indication divisional or number missing) the deficiency may be corrected consistent with the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement for divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application must be filed in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not filed in English the application is not accorded the date of filing of the parent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Contracting States in divisional limited to parent's designations
rubrics_metrics.description: In the divisional application only such Contracting States may be designated as were validly designated in the parent application on the date the divisional is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation of other states is without effect and applicant is notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for divisional: filing, designation, renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing and designation fees for the divisional must be paid within 21 days after filing; renewal fees for divisional are payable to ARIPO and are calculated from the parent's filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If renewal fees for parent have fallen due when divisional is filed, they must also be paid for the divisional within 21 days. Late payment may be made within six months with surcharge. Same applies if further renewal fees fall due at filing of divisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorizations for representatives filing divisional
rubrics_metrics.description: If representative must file an authorization, an individual authorization filed for the parent application may be valid for divisional only if it expressly empowers him to file divisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions on authorizations apply with regard to the divisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination of divisional same as other applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal examination of divisional applications is carried out as for other applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions apply including those relating to nucleotide or amino acid sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further procedure for divisionals: search, publication, examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional applications are searched, published and examined in the same way as other ARIPO patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant required to file request for examination and pay search and examination fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition certificate for displayed inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant states invention was displayed at an official international exhibition, he must file a certificate of exhibition within four months of filing the ARIPO application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate must be issued during exhibition by authority responsible for IP at the exhibition and must indicate (i) invention was exhibited, (ii) opening date of the exhibition, and (iii) date of first disclosure if different from opening date. Certificate must be accompanied by an identification of the invention authenticated by that authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects in exhibition certificate may be rectified
rubrics_metrics.description: Formality Section acknowledges receipt of certificate and identification and draws applicant's attention to manifest defects if possible to rectify within two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is notified if certificate or identification not furnished within time allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological material deposit information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application concerns biological material and the applicant states deposit has been made with a recognized depositary, the applicant must submit name of depositary and accession number and, where depositor is not applicant, depositor name and address, within the earliest of specified periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits: (i) within 16 months of filing or priority (deemed met if submitted before completion of technical preparations for publication), (ii) if early publication requested, up to date of such submission, (iii) if right to inspection communicated, within one month. When depositor and applicant differ, applicant must also submit document showing depositor authorized applicant to refer to deposit and gave unreserved irrevocable consent to it being made available to the public. Depositary must be on the recognized list (Budapest Treaty IDs); list published in Official Journal. If missing information, Formality Section notifies applicant; deposit must be identifiable in application so later accession number can be traced back without ambiguity; further action is for Examining Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of deposited biological material to experts only
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may declare that deposited biological material is to be made available only to an expert until publication of application or, where applicable, for 20 years from filing if application is refused/withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration must be a separate written declaration (not in description/claims) addressed to ARIPO; if admissible, it is mentioned on ARIPO Form 25 when application is published. If so informed, biological material is issued only to an expert recognized by the Director General or approved by applicant. List of recognized experts published in Official Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings: WIPO ST.25 compliance and electronic submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide and amino acid sequences should be represented in a sequence listing that conforms to WIPO Standard ST.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listing preferably filed as part of the description but may be filed later (then not part of application). In addition to written submission, sequence listing must be submitted in computer readable form on an authorized electronic carrier or attached to the electronically filed application; computer-readable data must comply with ST.25 and be identical to the written listing; applicant or representative must submit a statement to that effect. Formality Section will inform applicant of any deficiencies in the written listing, electronic data carrier, or statement and invite remedy within two months. Failure to comply may lead to refusal; applicant may request further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion into national application procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for conversion to national procedures must be made to ARIPO Office, specify Contracting States desired and be accompanied by a conversion fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of fee the request is not deemed filed until fee is paid. ARIPO transmits request and a copy of the files to the industrial property offices of the specified Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating the formalities report and legal consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: After formalities examination, Formality Section issues a notification identifying all Harare Protocol requirements not satisfied and, for deficiencies that can be corrected, invites applicant to correct within specified periods and notifies consequences (e.g., application deemed withdrawn, priority lost).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits are either fixed by Harare Protocol or left to ARIPO discretion subject to restrictions. If deficiency not rectified within due time, legal effects follow. Where appropriate, Search Examiner is informed of refusals or loss of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of application before and after notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to receipt of ARIPO notification the applicant may amend only if the Formality Section has invited him to remedy particular deficiencies; during the period in which the application may still be with Formality Section the applicant may of his own volition amend description, claims and drawings but must not add subject matter extending beyond content as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities Section examines amendments filed after receipt of notification for formal requirements; such amendments must remedy the deficiencies notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of errors in filed documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Linguistic errors, transcription errors and mistakes in any document filed with ARIPO may be corrected on request at any time, subject to limitations where third parties might be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If error affects items third parties might rely on (e.g., priority claims), request for correction must be filed as soon as possible and at least in time to be incorporated in publication. Exception if mistake is apparent on face of published application. Corrections in description/claims/drawings must be obvious — immediately evident that nothing else could have been intended — and within what a skilled person would derive directly and unambiguously from the whole of the documents as filed. Not allowable to replace complete application documents with other documents applicant had intended to file with request for grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing and early publication option
rubrics_metrics.description: Application published as soon as possible after 18 months from filing or earliest priority date; may be published earlier if requested and filing and search fees have been validly paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If decision granting patent becomes effective before expiry of 18 months, application and patent specification will both be published early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of abandonment of priority on publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant abandons priority, publication is deferred provided notification of abandonment is received before termination of technical preparations for publication (considered terminated seven weeks before the end of the eighteenth month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is informed when preparations are completed and of publication number/date. If abandonment notification received after that time, publication, if not already taken place, occurs as if priority date applied but a notice of abandonment will appear in ARIPO Journal. Same procedure when priority right is lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing publication and withdrawal limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Application is not published if finally refused or deemed withdrawn or withdrawn before termination of technical preparations for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant withdraws after technical preparations terminated, non-publication cannot be guaranteed though ARIPO will try to prevent publication case-by-case. Withdrawal must be a signed, unqualified, unambiguous declaration; applicant may make it subject to proviso that content not be made public. Neither application nor designation of Contracting State may be withdrawn once a third party proves entitlement proceedings initiated and until ARIPO resumes proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of the publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication must contain the description, the claims and any drawings as filed, specify inventor(s) where possible, and indicate designated Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication shows as designated all States party to Harare Protocol on the filing date; definitively designated states (with fees paid) announced later. Publication also contains any new/amended claims filed by applicant together with ARIPO search report and abstract if available before termination of technical preparations; otherwise applicant's abstract is published. Search opinion is not published with search report. If request for correction of errors is allowed it must be incorporated. Pending requests affecting third parties must be mentioned on the front page. Prohibited material is omitted, indicating place and number of words/drawings omitted. Sequence listings filed on filing date published as part of description; those filed later published as annex to documents or patent specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate publication of ARIPO search report
rubrics_metrics.description: If not published with the application, the ARIPO search report is published separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT international-phase processing prior to ARIPO phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial processing and formal examination of international (PCT) applications in the international phase are carried out by PCT authorities under PCT provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless specific request from applicant, ARIPO acting as designated/elected Office may not process or examine an international application prior to expiry of 31 months from filing or earliest priority date. ARIPO has not exercised waiver in PCT, so a copy of the international application will be furnished by the International Bureau.
